clips.text_zh: 點解成日都係 pump 完先想追 BTC？之前橫行幾星期完全冇人理，一升 15% 就全部人衝入去。又係學費。🙏
clips.text_en_b1: You watch BTC do nothing for weeks and ignore it completely. Then it pumps 15% and suddenly everyone wants in. Why does everyone want to buy after the move already happened? This came up on /biz/ today and the timing feels painfully familiar.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread asking why people chase BTC after it already pumped
clips.text_en_b2: Bitcoin spent weeks going absolutely nowhere, and nobody gave it a second look. The moment it pumped 15%, though, the floodgates opened and everyone piled in. Classic case of chasing the move after it's already played out. Came up on /biz/ today, and honestly, watching the crowd scramble feels painfully familiar. Same script, different cycle.
clips.text_en_c1: Bitcoin spent weeks consolidating within a narrow band while virtually nobody paid it any attention, and the moment it ripped fifteen percent higher the retail herd piled in as though that were somehow a revelation. The pattern is as old as spot ETFs, yet people continue to treat a confirmed breakout as an entry signal rather than confirmation that the easy money has already been made. A /biz/ thread crystallised this exact frustration today, and the timing felt uncomfortably familiar, as if one were watching the same cautionary tale play out on loop. Tuition fees paid in volatility, every single time.
clips.text_en_c2: The choreography is almost ritualistic at this point: weeks of grinding sideways induce total indifference, and then a 15% vertical move on BTC drags every retail account out of hibernation in the same breath. The asymmetry is glaring — liquidity evaporates the moment a position becomes comfortable, and reappears precisely when the trade has already matured. Late entry at elevated prices, anchored to the recent high, is a textbook expression of FOMO dressed up as conviction. A thread on /biz/ surfaced today, and the cycle felt grimly familiar, as though the market's most reliable pattern is the one traders insist on reliving, tuition and all.

clips.text_zh: BTC、XRP、DOGE，跟住 maid 買就得，揸住就得。講到尾都係我廢，冇跟到。👍
clips.text_en_b1: BTC. XRP. DOGE. All you literally had to do was follow the maid. That's all you had to hold. Three tickers, one lesson, and I still managed to miss it. The thread was on /biz/ today and it stings.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread about BTC, XRP, DOGE and following the maid
clips.text_en_b2: BTC, XRP, DOGE. That was literally the whole playbook. Just follow the maid's positions and hold through the volatility. Three tickers, one straightforward lesson, and I still managed to miss the boat entirely. The thread surfaced on /biz/ today, and reflecting on it honestly stings. Nobody to blame but myself.
clips.text_en_c1: BTC, XRP, DOGE. The entire thesis could be reduced to a single instruction: follow the maid's positions, hold whatever she disclosed, and one would have captured gains that most discretionary traders squandered chasing laggard plays. Three tickers, one unambiguous lesson, and yet I somehow contrived to miss it anyway, which says rather more about my own process than about the markets themselves. The thread resurfaced on /biz/ today, and the sting has not subsided, particularly because no plausible excuse remains available to anyone who claims they were watching the space at all.
clips.text_en_c2: The arithmetic was unsentimental: BTC, XRP and DOGE, three tickers, one custodial maid, and the only actionable instruction was to hold. No discretionary judgement, no timing exercise, no narrative contortion — simply the patience to let an exogenous signal do its work. I missed it, as I so often do, not through analytical failure but through that particular brand of paralysis masquerading as scepticism. The thread sat on /biz/ today with the quiet smugness of an open secret, and the sting is not merely opportunity cost but the recognition that conviction, in its purest form, was the only asset I neglected to acquire.

clips.text_zh: 每個政府每間公司都要自己 AI，咁點解 GPU 同 RAM 仲有貨賣俾我哋？AI 咁重要應該一早炒晒。wtf。🧐
clips.text_en_b1: Every government and corporation wants its own AI. Why are GPUs and RAMs still available for common people to buy? Yes, they are extremely expensive, but we can still buy them. If AI is that important, supplies should already be gone. The post was on /g/ today.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread asking why GPUs are still buyable with the AI boom
clips.text_en_b2: Every government on the planet and virtually every major corporation is scrambling to build out its own AI infrastructure. So why on earth are GPUs and RAM modules still sitting on shelves for ordinary consumers to pick up? Granted, prices are absolutely brutal, but stock clearly hasn't dried up. If AI mattered this much, shelves should be empty.
clips.text_en_c1: If every sovereign government and Fortune 500 corporation is racing to deploy bespoke large language models, one might reasonably expect consumer-grade accelerators and high-bandwidth memory to have vanished from retail channels entirely, snapped up by hyperscalers paying whatever the market demands. Yet GPUs and RAM kits remain purchasable, albeit at eye-watering premiums, which suggests either that aggregate capacity is far less constrained than the prevailing narrative implies, or that institutional procurement operates on cycles invisible to ordinary buyers. A /g/ thread raised the question today, and the disconnect between rhetoric and inventory remains genuinely baffling.
clips.text_en_c2: If every government, every Fortune 500 boardroom and every sovereign wealth fund is purportedly scrambling to operationalise proprietary artificial intelligence, one would expect the upstream supply chain — GPUs, high-bandwidth memory, advanced packaging — to have been cornered, allocated, or otherwise withdrawn from the consumer channel long ago. Yet retail inventory persists, however eye-wateringly priced, which suggests either that the much-vaunted demand surge is more rhetorical than structural, or that production capacity has, quietly and counter-intuitively, scaled in step with appetite. A /g/ thread raised the paradox today, and the anomaly remains genuinely disquieting to anyone who takes the prevailing AI hype at face value.

clips.text_zh: 有 4仔仔話印度移民其實犯罪率最低、對經濟仲有淨貢獻，點解西方世界仲要睇佢哋唔起？似層層加工我識嘅嘢。ok。
clips.text_en_b1: Indians are always among the groups with the lowest crime rates along with Chinese, based on UK, Denmark, Netherlands, Sweden, Canada and Finland data. Net economic contribution is positive in several countries including the UK, USA and Germany. So why are Indian immigrants viewed negatively? The thread is on /pol/.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ thread asking why Indian immigrants are viewed negatively despite strong outcomes
clips.text_en_b2: Indians consistently rank among the groups with the lowest crime rates, alongside Chinese, according to UK, Danish, Dutch, Swedish, Canadian, and Finnish data. Net fiscal contribution is solidly positive across countries like the UK, USA, and Germany. So why does Western public discourse still treat Indian immigrants with such thinly veiled contempt? The thread is on /pol/.
clips.text_en_c1: Cross-referencing crime statistics from the UK, Denmark, the Netherlands, Sweden, Canada and Finland reveals that individuals of Indian origin consistently rank among the lowest-incidence demographics alongside Chinese diaspora communities, a finding corroborated by several peer-reviewed studies. Economic data further indicates a positive net fiscal contribution in the UK, USA and Germany, which makes the persistent Western condescension toward Indian immigrants difficult to defend on empirical grounds. Whether this constitutes rank hypocrisy or simply reflexive cultural gatekeeping is debatable, though the evidence itself is not. The discussion surfaced on /pol/.
clips.text_en_c2: Cross-jurisdictional data — drawn from the UK, Denmark, the Netherlands, Sweden, Canada and Finland — consistently places Indian immigrants alongside Chinese cohorts at the lower end of the crime-rate distribution, a finding robust enough to survive methodological scrutiny. Net fiscal contribution is positive in several economies, including the UK, the United States and Germany, where Indian-origin professionals occupy a disproportionate share of STEM and medical positions. And yet the discursive framing in Western media remains reflexively hostile, an inversion of the empirical record that suggests ideology, rather than evidence, is doing the calibration. A /pol/ thread laid out the data today, and the dissonance between fact and sentiment is, frankly, exhausting to witness.

clips.text_zh: GTA 6 個 Lucia 真係頂唔順，5 呎 2 細佬女一拳打暈 6 呎 3 大隻佬，仲要單手 reload shotgun。打 lol 都冇咁屈機。lol。
clips.text_en_b1: GTA 6 is fine but Lucia is immersion breaking. She is 5'2 and can knock out a 6'3 man with one punch. She can shoot and drive at superhuman levels and even reloads shotguns with one hand. The thread was on /v/ and people are calling it woke.
clips.source_hint: /v/ thread complaining about Lucia being unrealistic in GTA 6
clips.text_en_b2: GTA 6 is shaping up nicely, but Lucia genuinely breaks immersion for me. She's 5'2 yet puts 6'3 bruisers to sleep with a single punch, reloads a shotgun one-handed, and handles firefights like a supersoldier. Even ranked League matches don't require that level of plot armour. The thread blew up on /v/, with plenty of accusations of wokeness flying around.
clips.text_en_c1: GTA 6 is shaping up to be an otherwise competent open-world experience, yet the protagonist Lucia represents a genuine immersion-breaking problem insofar as her physical dimensions bear no relation to her combat performance. Standing at five foot two, she is depicted flooring six-foot-three adversaries with single punches, reloading a twelve-gauge shotgun one-handed, and engaging in vehicular combat with reflexes that would make any ranked League of Legends player blush. The /v/ thread has predictably devolved into accusations of corporate pandering, though the mechanical absurdity arguably warrants scrutiny on its own merits.
clips.text_en_c2: GTA 6 is, on the whole, a technical triumph — yet Lucia strains credulity at every available juncture. A woman standing five foot two renders a six-foot-three adversary unconscious with a single, anatomically implausible strike, reloads a tactical shotgun one-handed without apparent recoil management, and otherwise operates at a capability envelope that would embarrass an Olympic decathlete. The physics engine has clearly been subordinated to a particular aesthetic agenda, and the result is immersion-shattering in the most literal sense. A /v/ thread is compiling the absurdities today, and the consensus — predictably — has crystallised around a single, tired explanation that does the discourse no favours whatsoever.

clips.text_zh: 三個月減 45 磅，但肌肉同力量都冇晒，去 gym 真係頂唔順，深蹲一 set 心口就爆。仲要日日逼自己食嘢，鬼死咁辛苦。肥仔信睇到都笑我。🙏
clips.text_en_b1: I lost 45 pounds in 3 months but I definitely lost muscle and strength. Being at the gym kills me. I cannot lift heavy because my body will not let me. I get super fatigued. And the eating is awful. I can barely eat more than a couple times a day. The thread is on /fit/.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ thread about cutting weight and losing strength on a cut
clips.text_en_b2: Dropped 45 pounds over three months, but I'm pretty sure I lost half my muscle and most of my strength along the way. Hitting the gym these days is absolutely brutal; any attempt to squat heavy and my body basically taps out within a set. Forcing down calories is miserable, and I can barely manage a couple of proper meals daily.
clips.text_en_c1: A forty-five-pound deficit across twelve weeks sounds impressive on paper, yet anyone who has actually attempted an aggressive cut will recognise the collateral damage immediately: skeletal muscle mass erodes, neuromuscular strength evaporates, and what once felt like a moderate squat becomes a genuine cardiac event before the first working set concludes. Appetite suppression compounds the misery, since forcing down even modest caloric intake demands a discipline that borders on pathological. Former heavy lifters familiar with this trajectory would find the suffering darkly comedic, though the poster themselves appears to find nothing remotely amusing about the situation.
clips.text_en_c2: Three months, forty-five pounds, and the customary bargain that aggressive deficits extract from the underprepared: lean tissue and measurable strength both sacrificed at the altar of the scale. The gym has become an endurance exercise in itself, since the central nervous system, deprived of adequate substrate, simply refuses to accommodate heavy compound work — squats terminate mid-set as intercostal fatigue sets in. Refeeds are scheduled with the grim determination of someone forcing medication, because appetite, in a prolonged caloric deficit, becomes a negotiable rather than spontaneous phenomenon. A /fit/ thread chronicled the arc today, and any former heavyweight observing the transformation would, I suspect, find the spectacle rather less triumphant than the eventual social media post will imply.

clips.text_zh: 成日見人吹 Zeta、ZZ、CCA，根本唔同班人做，點解當正傳計？初代先係神作，呢班美國仔真係識條鐵。btw Gundam 00 我睇過三次。👍
clips.text_en_b1: Most people can't discuss Mobile Suit Gundam without mentioning Zeta, ZZ and CCA, which were made by completely different people and should be non-canon. It devalues the original masterpiece. Americans are bizarrely obsessed with Zeta, which was less popular than the original when it aired. The thread is on /a/.
clips.source_hint: /a/ thread arguing that the original Gundam is underrated compared to its sequels
clips.text_en_b2: Half the time whenever Mobile Suit Gundam comes up, people immediately jump to Zeta, ZZ, or Char's Counterattack, as though those are the actual main entries. They were produced by entirely different staff and should arguably be treated as separate continuities, yet they constantly overshadow the masterpiece that started it all. Baffles me. The thread is on /a/.
clips.text_en_c1: It is genuinely curious how a substantial portion of Western Gundam discourse fixates upon Zeta, ZZ and Char's Counterattack as though these productions constituted the canonical baseline, when in fact each was helmed by entirely different creative teams and could reasonably be classified as derivative continuity rather than foundational canon. The original 1979 series remains, by virtually any critical measure, the work whose design philosophy and political undertones everything else merely extends. American audiences' peculiar fixation on Tomino's later projects, which underperformed the original in contemporary domestic ratings, only reinforces this perplexing inversion of merit. Discussed on /a/.
clips.text_en_c2: The canonisation of Zeta, ZZ and Char's Counterattack within anglophone discourse is a perennial irritant, given that each was helmed by an entirely different creative team, under altered production mandates, and with no narrative obligation to the original continuity. Treating these successor works as canonical extensions effectively subordinates Yoshiyuki Tomino's foundational 1979 text — a piece of speculative fiction whose thematic density and anti-war register remain unmatched — to inferior spiritual successors. The American fixation on Zeta, which was in fact out-rated by the original at the time of broadcast, betrays a generational parochialism that resists revision. An /a/ thread revisited the argument today, and having watched Gundam 00 three times myself, I find the consensus considerably less settled than its volume suggests.
